correctness.rationale: For a standard 3D Gaussian the independent angular direction is uniform and the radial factor for the degree-4m integrand is (4m+1)!!. Expanding the trace-zero determinant in the Gaussian transform gives (1−2s₂t²−8 det(A)t³)^(-1/2); the terms contributing to t^(2m) choose 2j cubic and m−3j quadratic factors. The m=1 normalization is 2s₂/15. At m=3 the resulting affine polynomial is (5625+54000u)/1001. Its higher-order analogues have a strictly positive linear term for every m≥3. The real-root discriminant is s₂³/2−27 det(A)²; equality at the two extremes characterizes zero determinant and a repeated eigenvalue, respectively, and the fixed-s₂ trace-zero spectral circle is connected. Harmonic degrees zero and one have only one real fixed-L² shape up to sign and rotation. Read checker.py and its recorded 368 exact checks; no frozen code was run. The proof holds for all stated m, not just the checked cases.

originality.rationale: The numerical-shadow literature already provides the exact all-order transform of this same spherical quadratic form, not just a Gaussian analogy. Substituting dimension three, Dirichlet parameters 1/2 and trace zero, then extracting even coefficients by the binomial theorem, gives the identical positive-coefficient polynomial, including its order of first variation. Standard cubic discriminant and compactness identify the range and equality cases. The claimed full ordering is a direct corollary of the older general moment formula with the elementary range restriction; no independent new claim survives.
residual_risks: This establishes coverage by an older exact general formula; it does not assert that the 2014 paper explicitly names the harmonic shapes or prints the sixth-order constants, or that it is the earliest source of the underlying transform.
